summary: A column chart of a float array: one rounded bar per value from a zero baseline up to the largest value, scaled to the canvas, with optional labels under the bars.

values.doc: A float array, "@name" of resources.floatArrays (export it to let the host replace the data); values ≥ 0, any count: the tallest bar is the largest value

labels.doc: Optional category labels, one short string per bar ("M", "T", ...), drawn 11 dp under the baseline; fixed when the document is built, so keep the array the same length

color.doc: Bar colour (in mono the bars are onSurface outlines)

height.doc: Height in dp, labels included (ignored with fill)

fill.doc: Fill the space the caller gives it (fillMaxSize) instead of width × height; give it a parent with a size or a weight

pitfalls: values is the name of a float array ("@visits" declared in resources.floatArrays), not a JSON list: one loop draws every bar with arrayGet, so a host that sets the exported array redraws the chart, whatever its length
labels are text drawn when the document is built ($each over a list): a host can change the numbers but not the labels, so keep the array's length matching them
Bars are rounded at the top only: each is a drawRoundRect that reaches 4 dp below the baseline, clipped to the plot area, so the ends sit flat on the baseline
The scale is 0..max of the data, recomputed from the array: comparing two charts needs the same max, which this component doesn't share
Everything scales with componentWidth() and componentHeight(), read inline in each coordinate; it keeps the call out of pattern mode, which is fine for a chart drawn once or twice
